title: The Japanese VMU
body: The main menu, big font and clock animals of the first VMUs, sold in Japan in 1998, read from their own BIOS. Its clock has a cat's paw prints and a helicopter where the later VMU has a dog and a bird.

title: Sonic Shuffle
body: The logo screen redrawn from the Japanese disc, an unused NO CARD screen, and the sheet of cards and digits the game builds your hand from.

title: Metropolis Street Racer
body: Three screens from the European disc, and a small text font the game carries but never uses.

title: Resident Evil Code: Veronica
body: Nineteen screens from the Japanese and European discs, including the portraits and the condition monitor with its heartbeat. The disc also shows which save icon is Claire's and which is Chris's.

title: Search by any of a game's names
body: Games are now found by their other names too, like Jet Grind Radio for Jet Set Radio, and show their English title with the Japanese one beneath. The Japanese flag now marks only what's in the Japanese release alone.

title: Marvel vs. Capcom 2, and VS.COM
body: Screens from the Japanese disc, including VS.COM, the VMU program the game copies to the memory card, with its sprites and three more save icons.

title: Game pages in tabs
body: A game's screens, sprites, fonts and notes are now tabs on its page; press 1 to 4 to switch.

title: Save icons
body: A new page for the colour icons the Dreamcast's file menu shows for each save: 520 icons from 344 games, searchable in one grid.

title: Jet Set Radio, and its graffiti viewer
body: Twelve screens from the Japanese disc, including the graffiti viewer the game copies to the VMU, with its fonts and sprites.

title: Sprites, out from behind the scenes
body: The smaller art games draw onto part of a screen, like digits, fonts and faces, now has its own card on each game's page.

title: Falcon's course, scrolling down
body: Screens can now scroll down as well as sideways, starting with a whole lap of Power Stone Mini's Falcon game.

title: Power Stone Mini
body: The VMU game hidden in Power Stone's program: its title, portraits and the screens of its three minigames.

title: The Shenmue Goodies viewer
body: The VMU program from Shenmue's Passport disc that showed the Goodies.

title: Shenmue's Goodies characters
body: 213 animated Shenmue characters, the Goodies Shenmue Passport traded online until 2002, from the Neoseeker Shenmue wiki. Their timing hasn't been checked against the game.

title: Shenmue, straight from the disc
body: Shenmue's title logo and 70 Man Battle screens from the Japanese disc.

title: The VMU's own main menu
body: The screen the VMU shows with no game, read from the US BIOS along with its clock animals and fonts.

title: Shinseiki Evangelion: Typing E-Keikaku
body: Every VMU screen in Gainax's Evangelion typing game, the first Windows CE game in the archive.

title: Crazy Taxi 2
body: Every VMU screen in the US release, including the title's dancing flames.

title: The rest of Ikaruga
body: Every other VMU screen from the Japanese disc, including the chain counter and an unused Load screen.

title: Street Fighter III: 3rd Strike, straight from the disc
body: Every VMU screen in the Japanese release.

title: Browse by game
body: The archive now opens on a searchable grid of games, each with its own page. Old links still work.

title: The rest of Sakura Taisen 3
body: Everything else on the disc, including the minigame intros, and the faces now blink.

title: Soul Calibur's fighters
body: All 19 fighters, five poses each, decompressed from the US disc.

title: Sakura Taisen 3, with scrolling banners
body: The title, crest and character expressions from the Japanese disc, and the 23 special attack banners the game scrolls across the VMU in battle.

title: Shenmue II, straight from the disc
body: Every VMU screen in the Japanese release.

title: Power Stone and Power Stone 2, straight from the disc
body: Every VMU screen in both games.

title: Project Justice, straight from the disc
body: Every VMU screen in the Japanese Moero! Justice Gakuen.

title: Bangaioh, straight from the disc
body: Every VMU screen in the Japanese release, played with the game's own timing, and four it never shows.

title: Berserk, straight from the disc
body: Every Puck screen, played with the game's own timing, including seven new animations and six unused screens.

title: Bangai-O
body: The title screen and its animated robot.

title: Ryo Hazuki comes to life
body: Shenmue's Ryo Hazuki is now animated, and you can filter the screens by game.

title: Carrier
body: The title screen from Jaleco's survival horror.

title: Sega Tetris
body: The title screen, memory card screens and the full animated cast.

title: Title screens and the first animations
body: Title screens from six more games and the first animated screens, which play on hover and download as GIF or animated SVG.

title: Tony Hawk's Pro Skater
body: All 35 screens, from "Rad" to "U suck".

title: The archive opens
body: The first 128 screens, from the Puyo Pop Fever cast to Sonic Adventure.
